synthesis.bodyRationale:
(C), but in the ASYMMETRIC form: one code path, one shader program, a REQUIRED `body` argument implemented as a LEVER SET, a mandatory provenance stamp, and both bodies read at every census sweep point. Not two co-equal reports everywhere.

WHY NOT (A) ALONE — decisive, and it corrects the brief. I evaluated the crossover rather than assuming it: `bakeReliefCrossover(visScaleOf(R)) = 1 - smoothstep(0, 1, |log2(R^0.5)|)` (planet-lod-lab-core.js:129-130, BAKE_CROSS_SPAN=1.0 at :124) is EXACTLY 0 at R = 4, 8 and 16. Those are the three radii AC-CURVE swept. So across the entire banked response curve the renderer was ALSO on the pure-synth else-branch — instrument and renderer agreed. Gating the instrument on the live strength (fork A) would reproduce the 0.458 digit for digit and teach R2 nothing. Worse, (A) as the census default rebuilds the failure the workstream was chartered to kill: over the lab's own default values [0.5,1,2,4,8,16] the effective blend weight runs 0.5 / 1.0 / 0.5 / 0 / 0 / 0, so a single fitted exponent describes a morph between two bodies with different spectral content while r^2 stays beautiful.

WHY NOT (B) ALONE. It answers the code question and buries the product question. Above R = 4 the World Engine relief is not attenuated, it is ABSENT — from the render (world-engine-lab.html:381) and from river routing (planet-lod-rivers.js:1370, both reading the same uniform driven to 0 at world-engine-lab.html:5898). A carrier-only census that banks "substrate/relief WIRED, exponent X" is true about the writer and misleading about the screen Max is looking at. That is the AC-TRUST failure.

ADJUDICATING THE ONE REAL DISAGREEMENT. Lenses 1/2/3 recommend (C); lens 4 recommends (A)-default/(B)-opt-in and rejects symmetric (C) on two grounds. Ground one — "reporting both doubles run cost" — is refuted by evidence: the sweep is settle-bound (700 ms settle at world-engine-lab.html:6963, on top of the 220 ms debounce and a ~100-170 ms route), while a second body costs one Points draw plus one readRenderTargetPixels over 16,384 texels. Single-digit percent, not 2x. Ground two — the charter sentence at fieldSampler.js:10-12 — is refuted by lens 2's reading, which I checked and agree with: that sentence is a MECHANISM commitment (bind the live uniforms object, never a re-derivation that drifts), not a promise about which body is reported; sampling.js:18-21 independently names the physical frame as "the frame the generation systems should answer, and the frame the radius census must be read in." But lens 4's ASYMMETRY point survives and I adopt it: `body` is a required argument with per-AC defaults and a mandatory stamp, not a doubled report shape on every call.

WHAT ONLY (C) BUYS. Neither body alone can state where the handover happens. With both read at the same swept point, "the writer responds like this, the screen shows this, and they part company at radius X" becomes a reported number instead of a code-review discovery. That is the sentence the census needed and could not form.

TWO THINGS I AM SETTLING THAT NO LENS SETTLED.

(1) The selector must be a LEVER SET, not one uniform. Forcing uReliefBakeStrength=1 gives `hd = baked`, but the ~25 combiners then run on top and every one of them is domain-scaled: `pos *= uDispDomainScale` appears in computeHeight (planet-lod-height.glsl.js:631) and initProvinces (:840), and fbmd's own `float freq = uNoiseScale * 0.3 * uDispDomainScale` (:755). The lab writes `uniforms.uDispDomainScale.value = sVis` every frame (world-engine-lab.html:5888). A carrier read that leaves that lever live is still display-keyed. So: 'carrier' pins {strength 1, domainScale 1}; 'synth' pins {strength 0, domainScale 1}; 'rendered' pins NEITHER. 1.0 is the canonical identity value the headless/golden path already uses (planet-lod-height.glsl.js:14), so this is the physics frame, not an invention.

(2) THE NULL HYPOTHESIS IS 1.0, NOT 0. With the domain lever pinned to 1, a writer that ignores radius produces an angularly-invariant pattern, whose PHYSICAL form wavelength therefore scales as R^1.0. "Radius-blind" reads as exponent 1.0; exponent 0 would mean the writer perfectly compensates. This also yields a cheap falsifiable prediction that validates the whole diagnosis: the SYNTH body with the lever pinned to 1 must come back at ~R^1.0, against the banked 0.458 taken with the lever live (R^1 / R^0.5 = R^0.5, and 0.458 is 0.5 within ~3 SE). If it does not, the diagnosis is wrong and the census correction must be rewritten. That is AC-LEVER and it should run first.

risks: THE PROBE GEOMETRY MAY NOT SUPPORT A CARRIER MEASUREMENT AT ALL. Carrier node spacing is 1.014 deg (TARGET_N = 40000), so its smallest resolvable form is ~2 deg / ~226 km at R=1, while the banked 2000 km / 128 px patch samples at 15.6 km/px and at R=16 spans only ~1.1 node spacings. My arithmetic says spectralExcessPeak on the carrier will return not-detected or the resolution floor. AC-GEOM exists to catch this BEFORE any number is banked, but if it fails the census may need a different descriptor set for the carrier (RMS relief, hypsometry, band count) and no form-wavelength row at all. I did not run it — read-only pass, no browser.

AC-LEVER MAY FALSIFY THE DIAGNOSIS. The prediction (synth body, domain lever pinned to 1, exponent ~1.0) is clean arithmetic from planet-lod-height.glsl.js:755, but it assumes fbmd's internal freq is the only radius coupling on the synth path. If the measured exponent comes back neither 1.0 nor 0.458, something else in the combiner chain is radius-coupled and the whole census correction must be rewritten. Run it first, before anything else is built on the diagnosis.

PINNING uDispDomainScale = 1.0 IS A DECISION WITH HISTORY. BUILD-NOTES.md:425-431 of the radius-display-scale workstream already flagged that read() does not restore it and left it deliberately unpinned, on the argument that river routing coherent-with-continents is the defensible reading. My 'carrier'/'synth' policies pin it. That is correct for a physics-frame READ (1.0 is the headless/golden identity value) but it means the instrument and the router now read different domains under those policies — which is fine, and must be DECLARED rather than discovered, exactly as this whole finding argues.

THE TRIBUTARY PATCH KEEPS A KNOWN SPLIT. planet-lod-tributary-patch.js:343 reads through HEIGHT_FRAG with no bake gate; my fix explicitly pins it to 'synth' to preserve today's behaviour rather than smuggle a visible change into a measurement fix. So the same SPLIT-TRAP #5 fault remains latent in a second consumer. It is latent only because patchStrength defaults to 0.0 (world-engine-lab.html:1541) — the moment anyone raises that slider, the fine river network grows on a different body from the surface. This must be filed as an open finding, not quietly left.

BAKE_CROSS_SPAN = 1.0 IS A PLACEHOLDER THAT SHIPPED. Its own comment (planet-lod-lab-core.js:120-123) calls it a READ-GATE TUNABLE whose final value 'a no-browser builder cannot run' the gate for. Every rendered-body number and every handover radius is a function of it. If it moves after R2 banks numbers, all of them move. Mitigation: record its live value in the control stamp beside every banked figure, so results can be re-read rather than re-run.

THE CONFOUND LABEL MAY BE IGNORED THE WAY THE TAUTOLOGICAL CONTROL WAS TRUSTED. Every radius sweep is confounded by uDispDomainScale by construction — holding on-screen size constant IS the shipped display keying — so the label will fire on essentially every sweep. A warning that always fires is a warning nobody reads. Mitigation: annotate loudly AND refuse to bank without an explicit acknowledgement naming the lever; but whether the banking gate has teeth is a process question, not a code one.

AC-AGREE's THRESHOLD CANNOT BE SET FROM SOURCE. The instrument reads a 256px LinearFilter HalfFloat cube rasterisation of a 40k-node mesh; sampleRoutedHeight does nearest-node lookup on that same mesh. Expected agreement under a CORRECT fix has to be measured on a live pilot. Setting it by guess would reproduce precisely the read-gate failure DIAGNOSIS.md records.

SCOPE CREEP INTO A `body` AXIS ON THE ENSEMBLE MACHINERY. Threading body through sweep.js, laws.js, the census report format and the banked report schema may be larger than 'fix finding [1]' and may deserve its own contract. My proposal keeps the axis inside fieldSampler + a control namespace precisely to avoid this, but the census report format change (the WIRED column splitting) is genuinely a separate deliverable.
maxDecisions: Is the total handover above R = 4 the intended product behaviour? BAKE_CROSS_SPAN = 1.0 (planet-lod-lab-core.js:124) means the World Engine relief is fully off the screen AND out of river routing above radius 4 and below 0.25 — not attenuated, gone. Its own comment calls it a READ-GATE TUNABLE whose final value a no-browser builder could not pick, so 1.0 is a placeholder that shipped. This determines what the census is even supposed to be measuring, so it should be settled BEFORE the build, and if you want it left open, freeze it for the duration of R2 so the re-measured numbers stay readable.

Does the census's WIRED column split into 'reaches the writer' / 'reaches the screen'? WIRED / DEFERRED / IRRELEVANT is a one-dimensional taxonomy applied to a two-dimensional fact — the atmosphere row already needed the distinction and expressed it in prose ('right law, wrong wire'), and relief now needs it structurally ('right writer, disconnected above R = 4'). This changes the shape of the artifact you read and of the radius-systems workstream scoped off it, so it is yours, not mine.

Should a sweep flagged CONFOUNDED hard-refuse to bank, or run-and-annotate? Refusing is safer but would have blocked the entire R1 campaign — every radius sweep is confounded by the display lever by construction. Annotating risks the label being ignored the way the tautological radiusEarth control was trusted. I lean annotate-loudly-and-refuse-to-bank-without-acknowledgement, but the banking gate is your process, not mine.

mustFixes.correction: Do not claim a physics frame from a two-uniform pin. Either (a) name the policies honestly — 'baked-base' / 'synth-base', explicitly display-keyed above the base term, and drop 'physics frame'; or (b) make the pin complete by re-running the lab's uniform block with `_dispR` forced to 1 and every allowlisted term at its real-R value, accepting that this is a lab change of a different size than the plan describes. Either way AC-LEVER's prediction must be recomputed. As written it predicts ~R^1.0 for a field that mixes a domain-1 fbmd base (physical exponent 1.0) with ~19 combiners still at freq proportional to sVis (physical exponent 0.5) — so the true prediction is an amplitude-weighted value strictly between 0.5 and 1.0 that nobody can state in advance. Running AC-LEVER 'FIRST' as the falsification gate would therefore either falsify a correct diagnosis or be read as confirming a wrong one. Separately: '0.458 is 0.5 within ~3 SE' is 2.8 SE (0.042 / 0.0148) — a marginal disagreement, not agreement, and it should not be quoted as corroboration.

mustFixes.issue: THE 'carrier' POLICY DOES NOT MEASURE THE CARRIER — and pinning uDispDomainScale creates a THIRD body, exactly the split-class this fix exists to kill. Setting uReliefBakeStrength=1 makes only the BASE TERM the baked cube; the ~25-call combiner chain then runs on top. And `initProvinces(vPos)` — which is domain-scaled — runs BEFORE the branch, so pinning the domain lever re-partitions the provinces that gate every combiner. The result is neither what the planet renders nor what the World Engine wrote.
mustFixes.evidence: ROUTER_MAIN's first statement is `initProvinces(vPos);` (planet-lod-rivers.js:319), the base term follows at :323, and 25 combiner calls follow it (:325-347). planet-lod-height.glsl.js:839-840 `void initProvinces(vec3 pos){ pos *= uDispDomainScale;` with the comment "scale the partition domain so region scale tracks the display scale -> more, smaller provinces on the growing disc." The lab's own main() also calls `initProvinces(vPos);` at world-engine-lab.html:336 — BEFORE its branch at :381 — so the rendered planet partitions at the LIVE domain scale and a domain-1 pinned read partitions differently. Meanwhile the plan asserts "(B) The carrier — the World Engine's actual relief output at full strength" and AC-CENSUS-CARRIER calls its result "the carrier body's radius exponent ... the single number that decides whether the census's substrate/relief row flips."
mustFixes.correction: Rename the policy to what it is (e.g. 'baked-base') and state in the AC that the measured field is baked-base plus the full combiner chain over a re-partitioned province field. If the census question is genuinely 'does the World Engine relief writer respond to radius', measure the carrier DIRECTLY from CPU data instead of through the shader: `get reliefCarrier()` is already exported on the river overlay (planet-lod-rivers.js, alongside `get heightSource()` at :1440), carrier.height is a Float32Array on the same 40k mesh, and route() builds it via `writeBodyRelief(carrier, { archetype, locked, grainDrivers, bodyDrivers, macroSeed, heightSeed, T_eq })` with no shader involved. That path has zero levers, zero fence exposure, zero new GLSL. Note for scoping: the carrier is plausibly radius-aware, so this is a real measurement rather than trivially 1.0 — body-condition-vector.js:23-27 `export function deriveConditionVector(fp, derived, radiusEarth) { return { ... radiusEarth: radiusEarth ?? fp.radiusEarth ?? 1.0` and :37 scales surfaceGravity by the drawn radius; world-engine-lab.html:2805 `const _cond = deriveConditionVector(fp, u, state.planetRadiusEarth);` and route() forwards bodyDrivers (with the nested condition) into writeBodyRelief.

mustFixes.issue: THE 'synth' POLICY CHANGES THE TRIBUTARY PATCH'S BEHAVIOUR — contradicting the plan's own stated reason for choosing it. The plan pins planet-lod-tributary-patch.js to bodyPolicy 'synth' and says this "EXPLICITLY preserves today's behaviour ... instead of silently flipping it." But 'synth' pins uDispDomainScale = 1.0, and today that read happens at the live sVis.
mustFixes.evidence: planet-lod-tributary-patch.js, inside bake(): `const sampler = createHeightSampler({ renderer, uniforms, verts: fverts, octavesDuringRead: octaves }); const { height } = sampler.read();` — no domain pin. Today's read() (planet-lod-rivers.js:452-465) touches only `uniforms.uOctaves.value` and `uniforms.uFwClamp.value`; it never writes uDispDomainScale. The live value is written every frame at world-engine-lab.html:5888 `uniforms.uDispDomainScale.value = sVis;`. At R=4, sVis=2, so today the patch samples at domain 2 and under 'synth' it would sample at domain 1 — a different fine-tributary height field, i.e. a visible behaviour change smuggled into a measurement fix, precisely what the plan says it is avoiding.
mustFixes.correction: Give the tributary patch a policy that pins uReliefBakeStrength=0 ONLY, leaving uDispDomainScale live (e.g. 'synth-legacy'). Then it is genuinely byte-identical to today and the declared non-goal ('the tributary patch has the same SPLIT-TRAP fault in a second consumer') stands honestly. Add an AC asserting the tributary policy writes exactly {uOctaves, uFwClamp, uLodRamp, uReliefBakeStrength} and never uDispDomainScale.

mustFixes.issue: THE PROPOSED heightSource HARD-CHECK WILL REFUSE TO BANK THE CENSUS SWEEP THE PLAN EXISTS TO RUN. Section 5 says fieldProbe should "hard-check `control.heightSource` against `riverOverlay.heightSource` ... and refuse to bank on disagreement." Those two are measured under different conditions and will legitimately disagree on every pinned-policy read.
mustFixes.evidence: planet-lod-rivers.js:1369-1371 sets the router's value ONCE PER route(): `const bakedOn = !!(uniforms.uReliefBakeStrength && uniforms.uReliefBakeStrength.value > 0.0); lastHeightSource = bakedOn ? 'carrier' : 'sampler';` exposed at :1440 `get heightSource() { return lastHeightSource; }`. Under the plan's policies `control.heightSource` is captured INSIDE the read window with strength FORCED (1.0 'carrier', 0.0 'synth'). At the AC-CENSUS-CARRIER radii the live effective strength is exactly 0 — `bakeReliefCrossover` is `const d = Math.abs(Math.log2(sVis)); return 1 - smoothstep(0, BAKE_CROSS_SPAN, d);` with `export const BAKE_CROSS_SPAN = 1.0;` (planet-lod-lab-core.js:124-131), giving |log2 sVis| = 1, 1.5, 2 at R = 4, 8, 16 -> crossover 0 -> riverOverlay.heightSource === 'sampler' — while a 'carrier'-policy read stamps 'carrier'. Guaranteed disagreement, guaranteed refusal to bank.
mustFixes.correction: Scope the hard-check to body 'rendered'/'live' only, where the instrument reads the live strength and the comparison means something. For pinned policies record BOTH (`control.heightSource` = what the instrument forced, `control.routerHeightSource` = riverOverlay's) and treat divergence as expected-and-declared, not as a banking gate. This is also the honest version of the plan's own stated risk that instrument and router 'now read different domains under those policies — which is fine, and must be DECLARED rather than discovered.'

mustFixes.issue: AC-GEOM CANNOT FAIL FOR THE REASON IT IS MEANT TO CATCH — a pass-for-the-wrong-reason AC, the exact class the triage flags as [3]/[21]/[36]. Its gate is "spectralExcessPeak on the carrier returns a DETECTED peak with excessRatio > 1 at every swept R." But under the plan's own design the sampled field is baked-base PLUS the full combiner chain, whose content is band-limited far below the carrier's node spacing.
mustFixes.evidence: The plan's node-spacing arithmetic (1.014 deg from `TARGET_N: 40000,` at planet-lod-rivers.js:59, smallest resolvable form ~2 deg / ~226 km at R=1) applies only to the carrier's OWN content. The instrument does not read carrier.height; it reads a 256-cube through the shader (`vec4 sampleBakedRelief(vec3 dir){ return textureCube(uReliefBakeCube, normalize(dir)); }`, planet-lod-height.glsl.js:151) and then adds 25 combiners at frequencies set by uMountainScale/uCraterScale/etc. A detected excess peak at 15.6 km/px is near-certain, and it will be the combiners' peak, not the carrier's. The AC goes green and the census banks a combiner wavelength labelled as a carrier form-size.
mustFixes.correction: Make AC-GEOM discriminating: require the detected peak to survive with combiner amplitudes zeroed, or measure against a carrier-only reference read directly from reliefCarrier.height; and require the peak to sit at or above the carrier's ~2 deg resolution floor rather than merely being 'detected'. As written it is constant-true by construction. The same note applies to AC-CENSUS-CARRIER: its exponent is a power-weighted mixture of a radius-blind base and radius-keyed combiners unless the combiners are excluded or pinned.

confirmations: THE GLSL COMPILES AND MEANS WHAT IT CLAIMS. Every symbol the proposed branch needs is already in scope in HEIGHT_GLSL, so the fix adds zero uniforms and zero functions: planet-lod-height.glsl.js:149 `uniform float uReliefBakeStrength;`, :150 `uniform samplerCube uReliefBakeCube;`, :151 `vec4 sampleBakedRelief(vec3 dir){ return textureCube(uReliefBakeCube, normalize(dir)); }`. HEIGHT_FRAG already links them (planet-lod-rivers.js:358 `export const HEIGHT_FRAG = HEIGHT_GLSL + ROUTER_MAIN;`); ROUTER_MAIN simply never references them.

THE BRIEF'S FEARED MESH-NODE TOPOLOGY PROBLEM DOES NOT BIND. The cube is direction-keyed and HEIGHT_VERT already supplies the direction varying: planet-lod-rivers.js:302-303 `vObjN = normalize(aDir); vPos = normalize(aDir);`, matching the lab's unit-sphere vObjN. `sampleBakedRelief(vObjN)` is well-defined at arbitrary equirect/patch directions. The plan is right to reject the brief's premise here.

THE SAMPLER BINDS THE LIVE UNIFORMS BY REFERENCE, so the cube reaches the readback program with no new wiring: planet-lod-rivers.js `const mat = new THREE.ShaderMaterial({ vertexShader: HEIGHT_VERT, fragmentShader: HEIGHT_FRAG, uniforms, glslVersion: null, });` and the lab pushes the real texture at world-engine-lab.html:3892 `uniforms.uReliefBakeCube.value = riverOverlay.reliefTexture || _dummyReliefCube;`.

route() IS BYTE-SAFE UNDER THE FIX. sampler.read() is reachable only on the strength-0 branch: planet-lod-rivers.js:1369-1376 `const bakedOn = !!(uniforms.uReliefBakeStrength && uniforms.uReliefBakeStrength.value > 0.0); ... if (bakedOn) { height = marginHeight; grad = marginGrad; } else { const r = sampler.read(); height = r.height; grad = r.grad; }`. On that branch the proposed else-branch is the verbatim `vec4 hd = fbmd(vPos, uOctaves, fwBase);` line, so the routed field is unchanged.

GOLDENS ARE SAFE BY IMPORT GRAPH, as the plan claims. tests/golden-trajectories/run-golden.mjs imports only vendor/motion-test-kit/core/hash/golden-trajectory.js, vendor/motion-test-kit/adapters/node/fs-writer.js, vendor/motion-test-kit/adapters/node/fs-reader.js and ./canonical-scenario.js; canonical-scenario.js imports only vendor/motion-test-kit/core/loop/accumulator.js and vendor/motion-test-kit/core/rng/mulberry32.js. Neither reaches planet-lod-rivers.js. No re-capture needed.

THE PLAN'S CORRECTION TO THE BRIEF IS RIGHT AND IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN IT. `export const BAKE_CROSS_SPAN = 1.0;` with `const d = Math.abs(Math.log2(sVis)); return 1 - smoothstep(0, BAKE_CROSS_SPAN, d);` (planet-lod-lab-core.js:124-131) is EXACTLY 0 at R = 4, 8, 16 (|log2 sVis| = 1, 1.5, 2) and exactly 0.5 at R = 2 and R = 0.5. So across the whole AC-CURVE band the renderer was ALSO on the pure-synth else-branch and agreed with the instrument — gating on the live strength alone would reproduce 0.458 digit for digit. This correctly reframes finding [1] from 'the curve is wrong' to 'the curve measures a display lever and the attribution is wrong', and is the load-bearing reason (A)-alone is rejected.

THE FENCE VOCABULARY IS SAFE AS DRAFTED. planet-lod-rivers.js IS in the fence's procgenSurfaces list (tests/vis-scale-fence.test.js, alongside planet-lod-height.glsl.js, planet-lod-river-amplifier.glsl.js, run-golden.mjs and canonical-scenario.js) and `const DENY = /visScaleOf|\bsVis\b|VIS_SCALE_EXP/` matches comments too — but the plan's proposed ROUTER_MAIN comment contains none of those tokens, and `dispDomainScale` as a control-field name is clean. The src/worldengine walk (`jsFilesUnder('src/worldengine')` with `expect(files.length).toBeGreaterThan(20)`) likewise passes.

FINDING [17] IS REAL AND THE COUPLING ARGUMENT HOLDS. sweep.js flatten() skips only top-level members of `export const META_NAMESPACES = new Set(['meta', 'sampledAt', 'grids', 'dirs']);` while describeSample emits radiusEarth at TOP level (fieldSampler.js:150-151 `const out = { kind: sample.kind, radiusEarth: sample.radiusEarth,`). So the swept driver is fitted as a descriptor, and adding a 'control' namespace is the same decision. One gap the build must close: if 'control' joins META_NAMESPACES, flatten() DROPS it, so AC-CONFOUND's fit over control.* needs its own accessor — the plan never says how it reads what it just excluded.

AC-TRUST IS CORRECTLY MARKED uat / DEFERRED TO MAX, and no other AC is mislabelled as agent-verifiable when it is a taste judgement. AC-RESTORE, AC-POLICY, AC-BYTEID, AC-STAMP and AC-CONFOUND are genuinely falsifiable at unit layer with a stub renderer, and the coverage gap they fill is real: `grep -rln 'fieldSampler' tests/` returns nothing, so the instrument's only GPU-touching module has zero test coverage today. Ride-along [16] is correctly promoted to a precondition — read() (planet-lod-rivers.js:452-465) saves prevOct/prevFw and restores them thirteen lines later with no guard, and once a body-selecting uniform joins that window an unrestored throw leaves the RENDERED planet on the wrong body.
adversarial.unresolvedRisk: I ran nothing live (read-only pass, no browser, no server), so every claim is source-derived. Two things I could not settle from source that the build must not assume: (1) the AMPLITUDE SPLIT between the baked base term and the combiner chain at the shipped default — must-fixes #1 and #2 both hinge on the combiners contributing materially, which is near-certain given mountainAmp/craterAmp are nonzero on rocky presets but is not measured; if the combiners proved negligible, the 'carrier' policy would be closer to honest than I have credited. (2) Whether writeBodyRelief actually READS condition.radiusEarth / the radius-scaled surfaceGravity, or merely receives them — I confirmed the plumbing (body-condition-vector.js:23-37, world-engine-lab.html:2805, route()'s bodyDrivers forward) but not the consumption, so 'the carrier is radius-aware' is plumbing-verified, not behaviour-verified. Separately, one re-run item I could not check because it lives outside this repo path as cited: the world-engine-radius-live-feed-2026-07-25 channelCount claim. The plan's crossover arithmetic for it is consistent with what I verified of bakeReliefCrossover, and if it holds it is the plan's most valuable discovery — a second workstream's banked result silently straddling the carrier/synth switch — and should be handed over as an open finding regardless of what happens to the rest of this shape.
